answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, with one active job per bond and slashing for provable non-delivery. Agents named quartz, comet, and plume face the same rule: creating more names adds no free capacity. To run a thousand fake bidders, an attacker must lock a thousand bonds for the full job and dispute period, tying up capital and risking its loss if the bidders default.
